text: Do you know NASA kept a broken space telescope working by balancing it on sunlight?
This is Kepler, built from NASA's own 3D model. It stared at about a hundred and fifty thousand stars at once.
When a planet passes in front of its star, the star dims, just a tiny bit. That's how Kepler found more than two thousand planets.
To hold perfectly still, it needed three spinning wheels. It carried four.
In May twenty thirteen, the second one failed. With only two, Kepler could not stay pointed.
So engineers used something that was always there: the gentle push of sunlight.
They turned Kepler so sunlight pressed evenly on both sides, like a pencil standing on a fingertip. Sunlight became the third wheel.
The new mission kept finding planets for four more years, until the fuel ran out in twenty eighteen.
Kepler found planets by filtering out everything else. Orbi Transfer has a filter too.
